q1_issues.issue: The result of "turn ... into sugars" is carried only by (Result (sk_turn $x) (sk_sugar $x)); the state-result shape also requires the reified result to carry an Experiencer naming what became it plus the flat copular atom, and neither is emitted.

Three Patient atoms are stacked on one turn event for the coordinated "sunlight, carbon dioxide and water", but coordinated NPs are distributive by default and the one-event/many-fillers collective form is licensed only for multiple Agent atoms on a reciprocal or aggregate predicate.

"Trees use photosynthesis" has a bare kind NP on each side, which is the stated mechanical trigger for an opaque kind-level relation (Use tree photosynthesis), yet the parse takes the distributing event-rule route instead.
The bare plural "sugars" is rendered as a single sk_sugar witness typed sugar, with no group encoding.

q2_gaps: a relational generic (bare kind on both sides) that also carries a purpose infinitive — the kind-relation form is one opaque binary atom with no eventuality for the purpose head To to attach to, so the relational-generic trigger and the purpose-connective rule cannot both be honoured

a many-to-one material transformation with coordinated inputs ("turn A, B and C into D") — the change-of-kind/state-result shape assumes a single bearer that is identical to the result state's Experiencer, and nothing licenses saying that several inputs jointly become one product
notes: The rule scaffolding is right: Skolem-function events per binding with no free variables, 0.9/0.9 for a bare empirical generic with no QuantifierPhrase, Theme for "use", subject control on the purpose event, main event first in (To ...), and the carbon_dioxide genus with the noun modifier unexposed. The defects are all inside the consequent, in how the transformation and its coordinated inputs are encoded.
